Nike holds basketball and loses football

How many of the top athletes in each sport have a contract with Nike Inc. (Nike, Jordan and Converse), in annual cuts from 2015 to 2026, and which brand moves explain the change.

Data as of October 1, 2026. Trigger: Kylian Mbappé leaves Nike and signs with On (Sep 18, 2026).

Top athletes with Nike, by sport and year

Sports are ordered by global audience, by my own judgment. Each cell shows how many of the top athletes have a contract with Nike Inc.; the blue intensity follows the percentage. Tap a cell to see the list: it shows the confidence of each data point, the n/a rows and the ? sign, which links to the source. The Prospect tag marks athletes aged 23 or under in the 2025–2026 cuts, whatever their brand.

Intensity = Nike % of total Dashed line = cut pending verified with source no conclusion, hypothesis no conclusion, brand not determined

Transfer market: key moves

Departures from and arrivals at Nike, renewals of top athletes and relevant moves between other brands since 2015. The Prospect tag marks athletes aged 23 or under at the time of the move. A cause is stated only when a source reports it; the ? sign links to each source.

Why almost all arrivals are renewals: Nike tends to sign its stars before they become stars (Mbappé at 9, Ingebrigtsen at 17, Scheffler before reaching number 1). Its important moves are extensions, lifetime deals or promotions to a signature shoe, not transfers from another brand.

Top 5 per sport. Brands outside the main group (Nike, Jordan, Converse, Adidas, Puma, Under Armour, On, New Balance, ASICS, Anta, Li-Ning) appear as "Other", with the name next to it. HM = honorable mention, not counted in the total. The ? sign links to the source.

What Nike spends on marketing

NKE demand creation expense, fiscal years ending in May. Source: FiscalAI (financial statements as reported); the "10-K" link opens the exact filing page in FiscalAI.

Demand creation includes advertising, promotion and sports marketing (endorsement contracts, free product and events). It does not isolate payments to individual athletes.

Endorsement contract commitments

Minimum payment obligations (base compensation and guaranteed minimum royalties) to athletes, public figures, teams and leagues, per the 10-K. Read in FiscalAI (filing_pdf); FiscalAI has no structured field or audit link for this figure, so the link goes to the 10-K on SEC.

Since the FY2025 10-K the figure includes "related marketing commitments", so FY2025–FY2026 are not directly comparable with FY2023–FY2024. Actual payments can be higher (performance bonuses, royalties) or lower (performance-based reduction clauses).

What the data says

Where Nike has a strong presence

  • Basketball: half or more of the All-NBA in every cut, with SGA, Wembanyama, Dončić and Cunningham in signature shoes.
  • Golf: has the OWGR number 1 in every cut since 2022 (Scheffler or McIlroy), and both as 1 and 2 in 2026.
  • Tennis, at the top: Sinner and Alcaraz, the two best players on tour.
  • Prospects: 5 of 15 athletes aged 23 or under in 2025–2026 (Mirra Andreeva, Victor Wembanyama, Carlos Alcaraz, Cole Palmer and Salma Paralluelo).

Where it is weak or falling

  • Football: went from 7/10 in 2023 to 3/10 in 2025; Adidas has 6 of the 2025 top 10 and the youngest prospects (Yamal and Cubarsí, 19). Mbappé, Kane and Lewandowski (4F, 2021) left.
  • NFL: from 3/5 in 2025 to 1/5 in 2026 after losing Josh Allen (New Balance) and McCaffrey (While On Earth); Burrow has worn Alo since 2024 and Stafford, johnnie-O since Mar 2026.
  • Athletics: none of the 2025 Athlete of the Year finalists has a Nike contract (0/6): Duplantis is Puma; Furlani and the distance runners, Adidas.
  • Tennis, in depth: beyond Sinner and Alcaraz, it lost Fritz, Rublev, Tiafoe, Draper, Musetti and Raducanu.
  • Baseball: low presence, held up by Jordan Brand (Judge and Betts).

Who gains what Nike loses: Adidas in football; On (with equity as part of the pay) in tennis and with Mbappé and El Bakkali; new or own brands in the NFL and basketball (New Balance, While On Earth, 741, 361).

What the 10-K says: Nike is not cutting what it commits to athletes. Endorsement obligations payable within 12 months have held at US$1.6–1.7B since FY2024, and the FY2026 10-K lists the growing influence of athletes' personal brands as a risk.

Open question: these data cannot tell whether Nike is reallocating money to fewer names or losing bidding contests; there are cases of both (Yamal and, according to The Athletic, Mbappé chose another brand; Harden, Federer and Rublev left because Nike did not match or did not renew). On Mbappé the sources contradict each other.

Data quality: 454 of 462 rows verified with a source. 5 remain without conclusion (hypothesis) and 3 without a determined brand; none changes the reading by sport.
